subject: Cloud Computing
title: Data Lakehouse Architecture
description: A quick win: understand Data Lakehouse Architecture.

hook.text: Data lakes are cheap but messy. Data warehouses are structured but expensive. The lakehouse combines both.

buildup.text: A data lakehouse applies warehouse-like structure to data lake storage. Structured queries on cheap, raw data.

discovery.text: Technologies like Delta Lake, Apache Iceberg, and Apache Hudi add ACID transactions to data lake files.

twist.text: Databricks and Snowflake are battling for the lakehouse market. Their architectures are converging from opposite sides.

climax.text: The lakehouse may replace both lakes and warehouses as the unified standard for cloud analytics.

punchline.text: Lake and warehouse merge. The lakehouse is the future of analytics.

quiz.question: What problem does the data lakehouse architecture solve?
options: It combines the low cost of data lakes with the structure of data warehouses
It eliminates the need for any data storage in the cloud
It only works with real-time streaming data

details.summary: A data lakehouse combines the low-cost storage and flexibility of a data lake with the query performance and governance of a data warehouse. Technologies like Delta Lake, Apache Iceberg, and Apache Hudi add ACID transactions and schema enforcement to lake storage.
details.whyItMatters: The lakehouse architecture eliminates the need to maintain separate lake and warehouse systems, reducing data duplication, cost, and the complexity of keeping both in sync.
takeaways: Combines data lake flexibility with warehouse performance
ACID transactions on open file formats like Parquet
Eliminates expensive data duplication between lake and warehouse

faq.question: How does a lakehouse differ from a data lake?
faq.answer: A data lake stores raw files without transaction guarantees or schema enforcement. A lakehouse adds a metadata layer that provides ACID transactions, time travel, schema evolution, and fast SQL queries on the same open-format files stored in the lake.

faq.question: Which lakehouse technology should you choose?
faq.answer: Delta Lake integrates tightly with Databricks and Spark. Apache Iceberg has broad engine support including Trino, Spark, and Flink. Apache Hudi was designed for incremental data processing. The best choice depends on your existing tooling and query engines.
